candidates.name: Peroneal neuropathy
support_spans: foot drop (tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus 1/5)
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and examination findings, including foot drop and absent Achilles reflexes, are consistent with peroneal neuropathy.

candidates.name: Lumbosacral plexopathy
support_spans: muscle strength nearly normalized, but lateral leg pain persisted
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and examination findings, including persistent leg pain and subsequent development of foot drop, could be indicative of lumbosacral plexopathy.

candidates.name: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP)
candidates.why: The patient's progressive symptoms and examination findings, including bilateral absent reflexes, could be consistent with CIDP.

key_evidence_spans: foot drop (tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus 1/5)

candidates.name: Peroneal neuropathy
support_spans: foot drop (tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus 1/5)
contradict_spans: Lumbar MRI demonstrated a right‐sided disc herniation at L5–S1 without significant nerve‐root or cord compression
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of foot drop and numbness in the lower extremity are consistent with peroneal neuropathy, which may not be directly related to the lumbar disc herniation
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked in favor of more common causes of lower extremity weakness, such as lumbar radiculopathy

candidates.name: Vasculitic neuropathy
support_spans: ankle‐brachial indices were decreased (0.78 on the right, 0.73 on the left)
contradict_spans: lower‐extremity arteriography showed no significant vascular lesions
candidates.why: The decreased ankle-brachial indices suggest possible vascular disease, which could be causing neuropathy, despite the lack of significant lesions on arteriography
candidates.protected_reason: Vasculitic neuropathy is a rare condition that may be missed if not considered in the differential diagnosis

candidates.name: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP)
support_spans: repeat peroneal conduction studies failed to elicit an evoked myogenic potential
contradict_spans: initial peroneal‐nerve conduction studies revealed a motor conduction velocity of 51.5 m/s
candidates.why: The progression of symptoms and abnormal nerve conduction studies are consistent with CIDP, which may present with asymmetric weakness and areflexia
candidates.protected_reason: CIDP is a rare condition that may be underdiagnosed if not considered in the differential diagnosis
